Q: Why did /var/log/syslog grow to 35GB on Ubuntu 22.04 despite weekly logrotate? A:

Why would /var/log/syslog grow to 35GB despite rotation being configured? Under what circumstances would logrotate fail to rotate syslog?

So far nothing you've shown suggests that logrotate failed to rotate syslog. Instead, it seems more likely to me that you got a lot more syslog messages this week, therefore the file grew larger.

The log rotation schedule you've configured is not size-based. If it's weekly then it's weekly, no matter how large the file gets. So if you happen to have a broken service which produces 35 GB of syslog messages during the week, then you're going to have a 35 GB syslog file.

Q: neo4j data science library causes failure to start A:

When the Neo4j Graph Data Science (GDS) library causes Neo4j to fail at startup, the issue is usually one of the following:

  1. Version incompatibility

  2. Incorrect plugin placement

  3. Missing configuration settings

  4. Java version mismatch

  5. Insufficient memory settings

Check Version Compatibility (Most Common Cause)

The GDS plugin must match your Neo4j version exactly (major + minor).

For example:

  • Neo4j 5.x → requires GDS 2.x

  • Neo4j 4.4 → requires GDS 2.x (specific compatible build)

If versions don’t match, Neo4j will fail during startup with classloading errors.

Check your Neo4j version:

neo4j --version

Then download the compatible GDS version from the official compatibility matrix.

Verify Plugin Location

The GDS .jar file must be placed in:

$NEO4J_HOME/plugins

Do not unzip it. It should remain a .jar file.

Update neo4j.conf

Ensure these lines are added:

dbms.security.procedures.unrestricted=gds.*
dbms.security.procedures.allowlist=gds.*

Without these, Neo4j may fail or refuse to load procedures.

Check Logs (Critical Step)

Open:

$NEO4J_HOME/logs/debug.log

Most startup failures clearly indicate:

  • Unsupported class version

  • Missing dependencies

  • Memory allocation failure

  • Plugin API mismatch

Verify Java Version

Neo4j 5 requires Java 17.

If you see something like:

UnsupportedClassVersionError

You’re likely running the wrong JDK.

Check:

java -version

Increase Memory (If GDS is Heavy)

GDS requires sufficient heap and page cache.

In neo4j.conf:

dbms.memory.heap.initial_size=4g
dbms.memory.heap.max_size=4g
dbms.memory.pagecache.size=2g

Adjust based on your system RAM.

Summary

Neo4j fails to start after installing GDS typically due to:

  • Version mismatch

  • Wrong Java version

  • Missing configuration

  • Insufficient memory

  • Plugin placed incorrectly

The debug log will indicate the exact cause.
